title: Critical: SAML assertion replay allows RBAC elevation in Private deployments
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Several Private deployment customers reported an SSO/SSO-related escalation where a specially crafted SAML assertion could be replayed against the Private control plane SAML consumer and result in temporary RBAC elevation for the session. The same flow exposed gaps in audit logging (missing canonical user identifiers) and revealed a KMS-integrations edge case where encrypted session metadata could not be rotated if the assertion used a transient NameID. Impact: multiple enterprise customers (FinServCo, HealthAI Labs, RetailOne) reported unexpected privileged access tokens appearing in their session lists, and support tickets escalated to SEV2/SEV1 depending on the customer. This ticket tracks the urgent investigation, hotpatch, and medium-term hardening work across three areas: SAML validation, RBAC policy enforcement, and audit/KMS hygiene.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure a Private deployment with SAML SSO using transient NameID and default relayState behavior
2) Craft a SAML assertion missing InResponseTo and with duplicate SubjectConfirmationData timestamps (replay vector)
3) POST to /private/sso/acs endpoint with the assertion and an existing session cookie
4) Observe session profile updated with elevated roles in /private/admin/sessions and missing canonical_user_id in audit records
5) Attempt key rotation on KMS-protected session metadata and observe decryption failures for affected sessions
mitigation: Short-term: Disable SAML SP-initiated login for vulnerable Private tenants via tenant toggle (support action)
Short-term: Revoke affected sessions and force re-authentication; provide scripted revocation for impacted customers
Medium-term: Apply hotpatch to SAML consumer to enforce InResponseTo, audience, and nonce checks and reject replayed signatures
Medium-term: Patch audit pipeline to include canonical_user_id in all session-related log entries
Workaround for KMS: Re-encrypt session metadata using fallback key path that includes explicit key context (manual support runbook)
fix_plan: 1) Create hotfix branch hotfix/eng/ENG-4821-saml-validation with immediate SAML strict checks (InResponseTo, AudienceRestriction, NotOnOrAfter, SubjectConfirmationData uniqueness)
2) Add RBAC enforcement layer to reject any role elevation changes that are not accompanied by an entitlement claim from the IdP and add server-side guardrails in the session mutator
3) Update audit emitter to populate canonical_user_id and session_origin fields atomically before any RBAC mutation
4) Add migration to re-encrypt session metadata for affected sessions with explicit key context and rotation-friendly envelope
5) Run tests and deploy hotfix to canary set then to remaining Private tenants using phased rollout
6) Publish post-incident notice and long-term roadmap ticket for token model revisions (ENG-4900)
testing_plan: Unit tests covering SAML validation matrix (missing InResponseTo, incorrect audience, expired assertion, replay attempts)
Integration tests with simulated IdP asserting transient NameID and replayed signatures
End-to-end test in Private staging that mirrors customer tenant configs (custom relayState + KMS key contexts)
Chaos test: replay captured assertion against canary control plane to assert it is rejected and audit log contains canonical_user_id
rollout_plan: Canary: Deploy hotfix to 2 Private tenants controlled by us (internal-demo-1, private-canary-2) and monitor metrics for 2 hours
Stage: Deploy to a subset of affected customers who agreed to early patching (FinServCo staging, HealthAI Labs staging)
Full: Roll to all Private customers with explicit communication and support runbook
Emergency: If any telemetry shows false positives or auth regressions, revert and ship quick follow-up; maintain ability to toggle strict SAML checks per-tenant
postmortem_actions: Document root cause and timeline in Confluence (security/ENG-4821-postmortem)
Add automated assertion-replay tests to CI for all SSO providers (required for Private releases)
Audit all KMS usage paths for session metadata and standardize key-context usage
Schedule architecture review for token/session model and RBAC enforcement (owners: Security + Runtime)

notes: This ticket spans cross-functional ownership: Runtime (SAML consumer), Security (threat validation), KMS (keys & rotations), and Support (customer communications). Priority is to ship hotpatch with minimal auth regressions and full audit trail for compliance customers. All external comms must be reviewed by Security and Legal before release notes are sent.
